systems.name: DG Control Retrofit and Upgradation from Legacy / Obsolete Systems
systems.commercial_group: A. MSB Room / Electrical and Control Systems
systems.summary: Replaces ageing generator control panels with modern digital genset controllers that start, synchronise and share load between the diesel generators.
systems.function: The generator control panels (GCP-1 to GCP-3) in the HV switchboard room host the genset controller for each DG: start/stop commands to the engine local control panel, automatic synchronising and closing of the 6.6 kV generator breaker, active power (kW) load sharing through speed bias to the governor, reactive (kvar) sharing through voltage bias to the AVR, generator alarms and the data link to the PMS. The retrofit replaces relay logic, analogue load sharing modules and obsolete controllers while keeping the engines, alternators and switchgear.
systems.operating_principle: On a start request (operator or PMS) the GCP commands the LCP to start the engine, waits for rated speed and voltage, matches frequency, voltage and phase angle to the busbar, closes the breaker within the synchronising window and ramps the set onto load. In parallel operation the controllers share kW in isochronous load sharing (or droop as back-up) and kvar by reactive droop or kvar sharing.

systems.name: Power Management System Upgradation
systems.commercial_group: A. MSB Room / Electrical and Control Systems
systems.summary: The power management system keeps enough generators online, shares load, sheds non-essential loads on overload and restores power after a blackout.
systems.function: Redundant PMS controllers in the HV switchboard room supervise the three 6.6 kV DGs, the bus tie and the LV MSB feeders. Functions: automatic start and stop of standby sets on load, heavy consumer start permission (cargo pumps), load sharing supervision, preferential trip and multi-stage load shedding, blackout detection and automatic restart, standby order selection. Operator stations are in the ECR and CCR.
systems.operating_principle: The PMS continuously compares online generator capacity with measured load. Above the start threshold it starts the next standby set; below the stop threshold it stops a set after a delay if the remaining sets stay below a safe load. On a generator trip or frequency drop it sheds loads by priority. On a dead bus it starts standby sets, closes the first set onto the dead bus, synchronises the others and reconnects essential consumers in sequence.

On the starboard wall the 6.6 kV MV switchboard lineup is seen from its front side (panels PTA to CP2, with the numerical protection relays on the panel doors; relay faces 69 to 75 deg from the eye); on the port wall the generator control panels GCP-1 to GCP-3 (59 to 65 deg) and the PMS controller cabinet beside them, with the operating aisle, cable trays and room fittings around them. systems.name: MV Relays - Testing, Calibration and Upgradation
systems.commercial_group: A. MSB Room / Electrical and Control Systems
systems.summary: Protection relays on the 6.6 kV switchboard detect faults and trip breakers; they are tested and calibrated regularly and can be upgraded from old electromechanical types to numerical relays.
systems.function: Eight numerical protection relays (IEDs) on the LV compartment doors of the 6.6 kV switchboard panels protect generators G1 to G3, transformer feeders TR1 and TR2, cargo pump VFD feeders CP1 and CP2 and the bus tie. Each relay measures CT and VT secondary values, evaluates protection functions (ANSI codes), trips its breaker and records events and disturbances. Testing and calibration are done through test blocks with a secondary injection test set.
systems.operating_principle: Each protection function compares a measured quantity with a pickup setting and trips after a defined time or curve. Coordination ensures the device closest to the fault trips first. Secondary injection testing verifies pickup, timing and trip outputs against the settings.

systems.name: Drives and Pump Controls
systems.commercial_group: A. MSB Room / Electrical and Control Systems
systems.summary: Variable frequency drives control the speed of large pumps such as the cargo offloading and ballast pumps, with control from the CCR and local stations.
systems.function: Two 6.6 kV VFDs drive the cargo offloading pump motors; 440 V VFDs drive the ballast pumps and sea water cooling pumps; the engine room MCC starts smaller auxiliaries. The drives are in the drives and MCC room; the motors are in the engine room and drive the pumps in the pump room through gas-tight bulkhead seals. Speed references and start/stop come from the ICSS (CCR) or local control stations. Large starts request PMS permission.
systems.operating_principle: The VFD rectifies the supply, maintains a DC link and inverts it to a variable frequency output, ramping the motor to the speed reference. Pump flow is controlled by speed instead of throttling. Protection in the drive covers overcurrent, overvoltage, motor overload and earth fault.

The ballast and SW cooling VFDs and the MCC on the starboard wall face the opposite way and are not in this frame; they are reached by orbiting or from the room list. systems.name: IGG - Inert Gas Generator Control System Retrofits and Upgradations
systems.commercial_group: A. MSB Room / Electrical and Control Systems
systems.summary: The inert gas generator produces low-oxygen gas to keep the cargo tank atmosphere non-flammable; its control system watches oxygen content and pressure.
systems.function: An oil-fired inert gas generator in the IG room (machinery space, outside the cargo area) produces flue gas that is cooled and scrubbed, then delivered by the IG main through the gas regulating valve, the deck water seal and non-return valve on the aft cargo deck to the cargo tanks. The local control panel sequences the burner, controls oxygen content, and switches between venting and delivery. Oxygen content and IG main pressure are indicated and recorded in the CCR; oxygen is indicated in the ECR and IG main pressure on the bridge.
systems.operating_principle: Two IG blowers supply air to the burner and deliver the inert gas through the scrubber to the deck main (arrangement representative; FSS 2.3.1.4.1 requires at least two IG blowers delivering to the cargo tanks, or one with spares for IG generator systems); combustion is adjusted to keep oxygen low. Gas is vented until oxygen is within limit, then the deck supply valve opens and the vent closes. If oxygen exceeds the limit the gas is vented automatically to atmosphere (2.2.2.4) and, in this simulation, delivery to the deck stops while venting (REPRESENTATIVE). The regulating valve closes when the predetermined shutdown limits are reached (2.2.2.2, 2.3.1.2.1).

It senses generator voltage, holds the setpoint, shares reactive power with the other sets through reactive droop or kvar sharing, and applies limiters (over-excitation, under-excitation, volts per hertz). The GCP/PMS provides voltage bias.
systems.operating_principle: The AVR compares measured voltage with the setpoint and adjusts exciter field current. With reactive droop the setpoint falls slightly with reactive current so paralleled sets share kvar.

arrival.note: Port aft part of the flat, looking down to starboard on the +y side of the alternators: the three AVR enclosures are seen from the front.

systems.name: DG Governor Controls Retrofit Solutions
systems.summary: The governor controls engine speed and therefore generator frequency and active load sharing; legacy mechanical governors can be upgraded to digital controllers.
systems.function: Each DG has an actuator on the fuel rack and an electronic speed controller in the local control panel. The controller holds speed (frequency), applies droop or isochronous load sharing, accepts speed bias from the GCP for synchronising and load control, and limits fuel during start and overload.
systems.operating_principle: The speed controller compares the magnetic pickup speed signal with the setpoint and drives the actuator to adjust fuel. In droop mode speed falls with load; in isochronous load sharing the controllers hold frequency and share kW through load sharing signals.

arrival.note: Forward end of the flat, looking aft: governor actuators at the DG-1 and DG-2 free ends and the DG-1 speed controller behind the glazed LCP door. pms_settings.governor_mode_basis: The PMS runs the DG governors in isochronous load sharing, so normal frequency stays at 60.0 Hz whatever the load and an underfrequency below 58.8 Hz indicates a real power deficit. load_shed_stages.trigger: online load > 100 % of online capacity for delay_s (2 s), or frequency < 58.8 Hz for 1 s (isochronous mode only), or generator breaker trip with remaining capacity below load (immediate, fast_delay_s)
still overloaded delay_s (3 s) after stage 1, or frequency < 58.2 Hz (isochronous mode only)
still overloaded delay_s (3 s) after stage 2, or frequency < 57.6 Hz (isochronous mode only)

pms_settings.blackout_restart: Dead bus detected (all bus voltages < 30 % for 1 s): heavy consumers blocked and LV feeders of priority 3 to 5 opened; all available standby sets start; the first set at rated voltage and frequency closes onto the dead bus (only one set permitted to close on a dead bus); further sets synchronise; feeders reconnect in priority order 1, 2, 3 in groups 5 s apart; priority 4 and 5 need operator reset. Target restoration time about 45 s (REPRESENTATIVE, not a rule value).

assumptions.text: Vessel is a representative converted VLCC style FPSO with internal turret, aft accommodation and aft machinery; principal dimensions 300 x 52 x 28 m from the reference package.
assumptions.basis: USER-SUPPLIED dimensions (reference README); arrangement UNVERIFIED engineering judgement

assumptions.text: Hull lines (hull_offsets) are simplified representative lines: immersed transom, stern taper, parallel midbody x 55 to 240, bow with flare and small bulb. Not a lines plan.
Double bottom / tank top at z 2.5 m; engine room flats at z 9.5 (generator flat) and z 18.0 (upper platform). Deck heights in accommodation 3.0 m.
Three 3000 kWe, 3750 kVA, 6.6 kV, 60 Hz, 720 rpm medium-speed DGs supply the hull 6.6 kV switchboard; 440 V LV MSB via two 2500 kVA transformers. All ratings representative.
Topsides gas turbine generators are context only; the PMS demonstration covers the hull DG plant. The hull/topsides interconnection is vessel specific and not modelled.

Governor speed controller is located in the DG local control panel (short MPU/actuator wiring); AVR is in an enclosure beside the alternator auxiliary terminal box. Both are common practice options; some vessels place them in the generator control panel.
Each DG engine is a 6-cylinder in-line medium-speed engine with one OMD head per crankcase compartment (6 heads).

3000 kW per set exceeds the 2,250 kW threshold in the MSC.1/Circ.1345 interpretation of SOLAS II-1/27.5 (OMD or equivalent as part of automatic shut-off for medium and high-speed engines). Whether the interpretation applies to generator engines on a given FPSO depends on flag, class and the scope of SOLAS II-1/27.5, whose text was not read in this task.

Inert gas requirements quoted (5 % O2 delivered, 8 % in tank, 100 mm WG low pressure alarm, CCR recording, ECR O2 indication, bridge pressure indication, non-return devices on deck in the cargo area, IGG outside the cargo area) are taken from MSC.367(93). Whether the FSS Code applies to a given FPSO depends on flag, class and coastal state.

Relay settings, PMS thresholds, AVR and governor values are REPRESENTATIVE educational values and must never be used as vessel settings. Real settings come from the vessel protection study and OEM data.
Equipment dimensions (cabinets, switchgear, VFDs, boilers, IGG, gensets) are typical envelope sizes for visualisation, not OEM dimensions.
Fire zone, A-60 boundary and hazardous area labels are representative. No hazardous area classification, fire integrity or escape analysis has been done.

Flare tower on the forecastle is chosen for maximum horizontal separation (about 230 m) from the aft accommodation. With the vessel bow to weather the forward flare is upwind of the unit, so radiation and any unignited or vented gas are carried aft over the topsides towards the accommodation and helideck; separation reduces but does not remove this. The flare base is about 9 m from the turret edge (representative). Location and height are decided by flare radiation and dispersion studies.

Helideck on the accommodation roof with the funnel aft of it. With the vessel bow to weather only the funnel exhaust is carried aft, away from the helideck; the aft helideck is downwind of the process area, flare and vents, so turbulence and hot or toxic gas exposure need a helideck environmental study.
PAGA uses two systems (A and B) in separate fire zones with interleaved loudspeaker loops in each area. Sound levels and intelligibility are not calculated.
Collision bulkhead at x 277 with FP at x 297 and Lpp 288 is a representative placement; the regulatory range was not checked in this task.
Mounted items (mounted_on) are positioned on their host; their own front access is through the host's access space and they are excluded from the 0.8 m clearance check.
Component size [Lx, Wy, Hz] is in ship axes (not rotated by facing). Facing gives the direction the operating face looks.
Cable routes are representative polylines along room trays, a central riser at x 23, y -1 and the main deck trunk at y -1, z 29.5; they do not model penetrations, segregation or cable sizing.

The IG main is routed from the IG room up the engine casing to the open main deck and along the open deck outboard (starboard) of the accommodation to the aft cargo deck, so it does not pass through accommodation, service or control station spaces (FSS 2.2.3.2.9, read in this task). The IG room door opens into the engine casing, not towards the ECR. Pipe routing is not modelled in 3D; compliance is not claimed.

deviations_from_reference.issue: Hull mesh FPSO_HULL extends to z 27 while the README states 28 m moulded depth.
deviations_from_reference.decision: Depth 28 m kept per README and brief; main deck at z 28.

deviations_from_reference.issue: Flare tower at x 56.5 to 63.5 (port), about 7 m forward of the aft accommodation front (x 49.5): worst-case location for radiation on the accommodation and lifeboats.
deviations_from_reference.decision: Flare moved to the forecastle (x 282 to 292, centreline), about 230 m from the accommodation. Basis: maximum separation. With bow to weather the forward flare is upwind of the topsides and accommodation, so the separation reduces but does not remove radiation and dispersion exposure; the flare base is about 9 m from the turret edge (representative). Radiation and dispersion studies decide the real location (UNVERIFIED).

deviations_from_reference.decision: Systems distributed over 24 rooms and open areas according to function (switchboard rooms, ECR, CCR, LER, telecom rooms, boiler room, IG room, generator flat, deck areas), with also_systems for shared equipment.

deviations_from_reference.decision: OMD heads on crankcase doors, OMD control unit beside each engine, governor actuator on the fuel rack, speed controller in the LCP, AVR beside the alternator terminal box (mounted_on).

deviations_from_reference.issue: The 22 m turret box lies inside the narrow bow (hull half breadth about 3 to 15 m there) yet is called external; an external turret would extend beyond LOA 300.
deviations_from_reference.decision: Internal turret, 16 m diameter, centred at x 265.5 in the full-breadth forward body, with turret space x 254 to 277 between forward cofferdam and collision bulkhead.

deviations_from_reference.issue: MV relays and the LV MSB are not distinguished; MV relays shown as one free-standing cubicle.
deviations_from_reference.decision: Separate 6.6 kV HV switchboard room (11-panel lineup with relays on panel doors) and 440 V LV MSB room with two transformers.

deviations_from_reference.issue: Field devices of PAGA, CCTV, ICSS, PABX and IPTV absent; ICSS, PAGA, PABX, IPTV, CCTV each a single rack.
deviations_from_reference.decision: Loudspeakers, beacons, cameras, telephones, displays, domes, junction boxes and transmitters distributed to the relevant areas and cabled to their racks.

deviations_from_reference.issue: Helideck cantilevered 8 m beyond the transom over a wheelhouse at z 51 to 59; bridge and accommodation heights inconsistent with 3 m deck heights.
deviations_from_reference.decision: Accommodation x 22 to 50 with 6 tiers to z 46, wheelhouse z 46 to 50 at the forward part, helideck x 20 to 40 at z 52.5 on the accommodation roof, funnel aft at x 8 to 16.

deviations_from_reference.decision: Main deck at z 28; process modules retained at the reference boxes on stools from z 30.
